children.topic: Cholelithiasis (Gallstones)
Types of Stones:
Cholesterol stones (80%): Yellow-green, radiolucent, risk factors = 5 Fs (Female, Fat, Forty, Fertile, Fair)
Black Pigment stones: Calcium bilirubinate, radiopaque, hemolysis (sickle cell, thalassemia), cirrhosis
Brown Pigment stones: Biliary infection (E. coli, Clonorchis), radiolucent, formed in ducts
Biliary Colic: Episodic postprandial RUQ/epigastric pain radiating to right scapula (Boas sign), duration <6 hours, normal LFTs & WBC
Acute Cholecystitis
Pathophysiology: Cystic duct obstruction → gallbladder distension, ischemia, bacterial superinfection (E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus)
Clinical Triad: Constant RUQ pain (>6 hours), Fever, Leukocytosis
Physical Signs: Murphy's sign (inspiratory arrest on RUQ palpation), tender palpable GB (30%)
Tokyo Guidelines (TG18) Diagnostic Criteria: A. Local inflammation (Murphy, RUQ pain/mass) B. Systemic inflammation (Fever, ↑WBC, ↑CRP) C. Imaging findings (US)
Imaging & Diagnosis
Ultrasound (1st line, 95% sensitivity): GB wall thickening (>4 mm), Pericholecystic fluid, Sonographic Murphy sign, Impacted stone in neck
HIDA Scan (Most sensitive): Non-visualization of GB after 4 hours = positive for cystic duct obstruction
CT Abdomen: Used if complications suspected (gangrene, perforation, gas)
Management & Surgery
Early Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (within 72 hours of symptom onset) = Standard of care
Conservative / Delay: NPO, IV fluids, IV antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole), analgesia
Percutaneous Cholecystostomy: High-risk/unstable surgical candidates unfit for general anesthesia
Bailout Options in Difficult Cholecystectomy: Subtotal cholecystectomy (fenestrating/reconstituting), Fundus-first (retrograde) approach
Complications of Cholecystitis
Empyema of Gallbladder (suppurative cholecystitis)
Gangrenous Cholecystitis → Free perforation (peritonitis) or Covered perforation (abscess)
Emphysematous Cholecystitis: Gas in GB wall/lumen (Clostridium perfringens), emergency in elderly males with Diabetes
Cholecystoenteric Fistula & Gallstone Ileus: Erosion into duodenum → obstruction at ileocecal valve (Rigler triad: SBO, pneumobilia, ectopic stone)
Mirizzi Syndrome: Stone in cystic duct/neck compressing CHD (Type I: external compression, Type II–IV: cholecystobiliary fistula)
